bham-01-tip.caption: The evenings are dark by four and the phone has not stopped. This is the stretch where the shop, the van and the chair are all busy at once, and the paperwork quietly stacks up behind the counter because there is simply no hour left in the day for it. That is the point of us. You carry on serving, driving and cutting; we keep the records straight, tell you what is coming and ask you for things one at a time instead of all at once. Washwood Heath Road is five minutes from most of Saltley and Small Heath, and WhatsApp is quicker than that.
bham-01-tip.ask: Send this to the one person you know who is working seven days this month.
bham-01-tip.title: The busiest month is the worst month for paperwork

bham-02-acq.caption: You should be able to get to your accountant and back before the shop reopens. Ours is at 22-42 Washwood Heath Road in Saltley, B8 1RB, which is a short drive from Small Heath, Aston, Erdington and Digbeth, and there is a human being in the room rather than a menu of options. Bring the folder, the carrier bag, the shoebox, whatever it is in. We will go through it with you, tell you plainly where your limited company stands and what the next step is, and you will leave knowing it. If coming in is awkward, message us first and we will sort it from there.
bham-02-acq.ask: Save this so the address is in your phone when you need it.
bham-02-acq.title: An accountant a short drive away, not a hold queue

bham-03-acq.caption: Cash takings on a Saturday. A van on finance. Three jobs in one week and then a fortnight where the phone barely rings. A chair rented out at the back. None of that is unusual to us, because it is what most of the businesses we look after around Birmingham actually look like. That matters more than it sounds. It means you are not spending the first half hour explaining your trade before anyone can help you, and it means nobody tells you your figures look odd when they are simply the figures of a real West Midlands business. Move your limited company over and start from the middle, not the beginning.
bham-03-acq.ask: Share this with someone who is tired of explaining their trade from scratch.
bham-03-acq.title: We already know what your trade looks like on paper

bham-04-acq.caption: Plenty of people put off ringing an accountant because they assume the first conversation is the start of something they cannot get out of. It is not. You can walk in off Washwood Heath Road with whatever has been sitting at the back of your mind - how you are paying yourself, whether the limited company is still the right shape, what the last set of accounts was actually telling you - and simply ask. We will tell you in plain words what we can see, and if you want to go away and think about it for a month, go away and think about it for a month. Nothing has to be posted, nothing has to be signed, nobody chases you afterwards. The first 30 minutes are free, and the only thing you have to leave with is a clearer idea of where you stand.
bham-04-acq.ask: Share this with the person who has been meaning to change accountant since last winter.
bham-04-acq.title: A first conversation that commits you to nothing

bham-05-edu.caption: Business rates are worked out in pence on every pound of your property's rateable value, and the pence are changing. In England, from 1 April 2027, the small business rate for shops, cafes, pubs and similar retail, hospitality and leisure premises is 39.5p, against 44.7p for a small business outside those trades. The standard rates are 44.5p and 49.7p. Who is left out: these are England figures only, so Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland each run their own system; vape shops and adult gaming centres are to be excluded from the retail, hospitality and leisure definition; and an empty unit cannot qualify for the lower rate. The regulations are still to come, so treat this as the position as announced.
bham-05-edu.ask: Save this for when your 2027-28 rates bill lands and you want to check the pence.
bham-05-edu.title: Two different rates, and which one a small cafe pays

bham-06-edu.caption: It is the season for dropping something off with a good customer, so here is the line that catches people. If you are VAT registered, you can give one customer gifts costing up to 50 pounds in total, excluding VAT, in any 12-month period, and there is no VAT for you to account for. The trap is the word total. It is not 50 pounds per gift. Three hampers at 30 pounds each to the same customer passes it, and VAT is then due on the cost of all of them, not just the amount over 50. And yes, a hamper or a bottle of wine is a gift of goods, so it sits inside that 50 pounds with everything else you gave that customer during the 12 months. What is a different rule altogether is hospitality you lay on yourself - a meal out, a box at the match - which counts as entertainment rather than a gift. Who is not caught: if you were never entitled to reclaim the VAT on the goods in the first place, there is nothing for you to account for, and genuine samples of what you sell are a separate rule with no cash limit at all.
bham-06-edu.ask: Save this before you order the Christmas hampers.
bham-06-edu.title: The 50 pound gift rule people get wrong every Christmas

bham-07-edu.caption: Most people who say they are going to get their Council Tax band changed do not realise there are two completely different processes, and only one of them lets you appeal. If you have been paying on the property for less than 6 months, or your band was changed by the Valuation Office within the last 6 months, you have a legal right to challenge. That is a proposal: a decision in up to 4 months, and if you disagree you can take it to the Valuation Tribunal, which costs nothing. Once you are past that 6 months, all that is open to you is a band review - up to 12 months to decide, and no right of appeal at all. Either way you must carry on paying your Council Tax while it is looked at, because a challenge is not a pause button. This is the England and Wales route: Scotland goes through the Scottish assessors, and Northern Ireland has domestic rates rather than Council Tax.
bham-07-edu.ask: Save this - the 6-month mark is the whole difference.
bham-07-edu.title: Only one way to challenge your Council Tax band lets you appeal

bham-08-joke.caption: Every shop plans for the rush and then gets caught out by something small. A queue on the pavement at six in the morning and a drawer holding four pound coins and a fiver is not the detail anybody writes on the plan. Here is the part that matters once the doors shut. The money that was in the till before the doors opened is not money anybody paid you, so if it is still sitting in the count, the biggest day of the year reads higher than it was and the day after reads lower. Note what you started with, lift it back out before you add up, and keep the card machine total as its own figure. Three numbers, written down once, on the night. A record day is worth getting right.
bham-08-joke.ask: Share this with whoever is counting up on Friday night.
bham-08-joke.title: The queue was there at six. The change was not.

bham-09-joke.caption: In nearly every family business there is a job that was never given to anyone. The buying has an owner. The till has an owner. The folder sits on top of the fridge and belongs to nobody, and then it belongs to everybody at the worst possible moment. The fix is unglamorous and it works: say out loud whose job it is, give that person one slot a week, and let them be the one who sends things on to us. The month stops being an event and becomes a habit.
bham-09-joke.ask: Share this with the family member who will recognise the folder.
bham-09-joke.title: The one job in a family shop that nobody claimed

bham-10-quote.caption: Written four hundred years ago and still the most useful sentence for a quiet end of November. Work does not only arrive; a fair part of it is made, by the call you place, the price you put in writing, the customer you ring back when you said you would. Trade is slow in places this week and there is time to make one or two things happen rather than wait for them to.
bham-10-quote.ask: Save this one for a slow week.
bham-10-quote.title: Four hundred years old and still true in a slow week
